Streets, schools and getting around Cambie

items.t: The corridor street is Cambie Street, crossed by West King Edward Avenue, West 41st Avenue, West 49th Avenue and Marine Drive; Oak Street is the parallel arterial west of Cambie Street. The Cambie Corridor Plan runs from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River.

Where the condo stock concentrates: at the Canada Line station nodes — King Edward (Cambie Village), Oakridge–41st Avenue (the Oakridge Municipal Town Centre anchor), Langara–49th Avenue, and the Marine Drive / West 59th Avenue end (Cambie Gardens, Belpark) — plus the Queen Elizabeth Park rise around West 29th–35th Avenues (Chelsea, Livingstone, 35 Park West, Lina, The Charlotte). The side streets between stations are primarily houses, duplexes and multiplexes under R1-1.

Transit: the Canada Line runs the length of the corridor along Cambie Street, with stations at King Edward, Oakridge–41st Avenue, Langara–49th Avenue and Marine Drive; TransLink route 41 runs via West 41st Avenue and route 49 via 49th Avenue.

Landmarks: Queen Elizabeth Park (52 hectares, 125 metres above sea level, the highest point in the City of Vancouver) sits on the corridor's east side at Little Mountain; Oakridge Park (the former Oakridge Centre site) anchors the south end at Cambie and West 41st.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cambie

items.t: City plan and zoning: the Cambie Corridor Plan (approved by Council May 9, 2011; Phase 3 approved 2018) guides growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River around the Canada Line stations; zoning is Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — side streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule (minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex; a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units), arterial sites on Cambie Street sit under the C-2 District Schedule, and station-area parcels are typically site-specific CD-1 districts.

District energy / geothermal charges: The Camellia's listings record geothermal heating — in buildings with ambient/geothermal or district-energy systems the utility charge can sit outside the strata fee.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cambie

items.t: The corridor is a plan, not a neighbourhood. The Cambie Corridor Plan was approved May 9, 2011, with Phase 3 in 2018 extending policy to the side streets within walking distance of the stations — two lots on the same block can carry different plan designations, and most corridor densities still require a rezoning application.

Cambie Gardens sits on the Pearson Dogwood site. Onni's master-planned community at Cambie and West 59th Avenue is a 25-acre site whose later phases may be purpose-built rentals rather than condos — the tenure of each new tower must be checked building by building, not assumed from Phase 1.

OPAL spans a whole city block — and three tenures. The 130-home OPAL community between Yukon and Cambie Streets mixes 44 strata condos, 56 rentals and 30 complex-care suites in three connected buildings; two units with the same address can have entirely different purchase documents.

Queen Elizabeth Park is the city's high point. At 125 metres above sea level atop Little Mountain, the park explains the view premiums on the West 29th–35th Avenue buildings — and why Chelsea was marketed across the street from it.

The Oakridge station itself is being rebuilt with private money. Reports on Oakridge Park describe a $27 million Oakridge–41st Avenue Station overhaul, $25 million of it privately funded by the developers — corridor buyers near 41st are buying into a construction zone and a town centre at the same time.

The corridor's north end is a hospital district. The City states the South Cambie portion is known for its medical facilities, including BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre at 4480 Oak Street — a distinct tenant and buyer pool for King Edward–area buildings.

items.t: Form B diligence (both strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level lines in (for example Aperture's pets line) are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Floodplain at the south foot: the City's designated floodplain is a citywide dataset covering coastal and river floodplains, and the corridor's south foot runs down to the Fraser River at Marine Drive.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cambie
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established side-street lots: single detached houses, duplexes and multiple dwellings under R1-1 on the corridor side streets, with ground-oriented townhouse and rowhouse areas under the Cambie Corridor Plan and apartment and mixed-use buildings at the Canada Line station areas and on Cambie Street itself. Freehold houses on the side streets; strata apartments and townhouses on the corridor and at the stations; purpose-built rental in the newer station-area buildings. The side-street pattern is historic subdivision fabric — built lots, not a lot offering.

Lot character, as the R1-1 schedule states it: minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m) and 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units, and a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house. Station-area and arterial parcels are governed by corridor plan designations and CD-1 or C-2 districts rather than those minimums — the C-2 District Schedule applies to arterial sites on Cambie Street and states its intent as a wide range of commercial uses and dwelling uses along arterial streets.
No ALR percentage split is stated — check any specific parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping.

Assemblies: on or near Cambie Street, the Cambie Corridor Plan, not just the base zoning, drives value. A buyer must distinguish plan designation from approved zoning, since most corridor densities still require a rezoning application.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Cambie

items.t: "Cambie" is a corridor and village name, not one of the City of Vancouver's 22 official local areas — the City's 22-area list contains South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge, the three official areas the corridor passes through, and no area simply called "Cambie." The City framework for the street itself is the Cambie Corridor Plan, approved by Council on May 9, 2011, guiding transit-oriented growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River, centred on the Canada Line stations at Marine Drive, Langara–49th Avenue, Oakridge–41st Avenue and King Edward; the City describes the corridor as its biggest growth area outside Downtown, and Phase 3 (approved 2018) extended land-use policy to the neighbourhood streets within walking distance of the stations.

Nearby areas: Shaughnessy and Douglas Park to the west and north-west (across Oak Street), Mount Pleasant and False Creek to the north-east at the street's top end, Marpole at the south-west foot, and Langara to the south-east.

Roads and transit: Cambie Street is the corridor street, crossed by West King Edward Avenue, West 41st Avenue, West 49th Avenue and Marine Drive; Oak Street is the parallel arterial west of Cambie Street. The Canada Line runs the length of the corridor along Cambie Street, with stations at King Edward, Oakridge–41st Avenue, Langara–49th Avenue and Marine Drive. TransLink route 41 runs to Joyce Station via West 41st Avenue and Oakridge Station, and route 49 runs from Metrotown Station to UBC via 49th Avenue and Langara–49th Avenue Station.

Civic anchors: Queen Elizabeth Park, atop Little Mountain in Riley Park — 52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level, the highest point in the City of Vancouver, with the Bloedel Conservatory, quarry gardens and an arboretum; Douglas Park Community Centre, 801 West 22nd Avenue, at the corridor's north end, and Hillcrest Centre, 4575 Clancy Loranger Way in Riley Park, on its east side; Oakridge Branch of Vancouver Public Library at the south end. The South Cambie portion is known for its medical facilities, as the City states, including BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital and Health Centre at 4480 Oak Street.
Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based and checked in the VSB School Locator / Catchment Boundaries tool; SD39 has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cambie

items.t: Plan / Zoning framework: the Cambie Corridor Plan (approved May 9, 2011; Phase 3 approved 2018) guides growth from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River, and the zoning instrument is the City of Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — corridor side streets sit under its R1-1 District Schedule (minimums), arterial sites under C-2, and station-area parcels under corridor plan designations and CD-1 districts. There is no separate "Cambie" OCP — the corridor plan is the framework.

SSMUH / multiplex potential as the City states it: under R1-1 a multiple dwelling may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units on a qualifying lot (minimum site areas 306 m² / 464 m² / 557 m² by unit count), and a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house — that multiplex potential is the side-street land value story, and it is parcel-specific.

Subdivision + servicing — City instruments: subdivision in Vancouver runs under the Subdivision By-law No. 5208, and its 2026 fees are set by By-law No. 14538 (enacted December 9, 2025, in force January 1, 2026), which substitutes a new Schedule F: Class I (Major) $174,300, Class II (Intermediate) $87,200, Class III (Minor) $15,020, Class V (Air Space) $125,100 where FSR is greater than 3.0, and Class VI (Freehold Rowhouses) $15,020 plus $1,950 per freehold lot. The City's major-subdivision process (sites over 10,000 m², or 10,000–40,000 m² likely to require complex legal agreements — expressly including bare-land strata proposals) requires a preliminary proposal with a current Land Title Office title search and a lawyer's charge summary, submitted to the Approving Officer.

Bare-land strata rules: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

Empty Homes Tax — vancouver only, applies here: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax is 3% of assessed taxable value; owners must submit an annual property status declaration, and the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date. Due diligence on any corridor purchase should confirm the seller's declaration status.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cambie

items.t: "Cambie" is a plan, not a place, in City law: the City has 22 official local areas and this corridor crosses three of them — a deed, a tax notice and a school catchment will all name South Cambie, Riley Park or Oakridge, never "Cambie," while the board search name and the Cambie Corridor Plan are what actually organize the market here.

The corridor's growth claim is the City's own: the City describes the Cambie Corridor as its biggest growth area outside Downtown, with Phase 3 (2018) extending policy off the arterial into the neighbourhood streets within walking distance of the stations — the off-arterial townhouse and low-rise forms are plan policy, not spot rezonings.

Vancouver's subdivision fee schedule is classed by legal complexity, not just size: the 2026 Schedule F charges $15,020 for a minor subdivision but $174,300 for a major one, and freehold rowhouses carry their own class (Class VI) at $15,020 plus $1,950 per lot — the fee class is an early read on how the City sees a proposal's legal-agreement burden.

The street was named for a CPR engineer, and its park is the city's roof: South Cambie was named after CPR engineer Henry Cambie, and Queen Elizabeth Park atop Little Mountain is 52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level — the highest point in the City of Vancouver — which is why the Riley Park segment of the corridor carries view value the flat Marine Drive end does not.
(The published CMHC range is 0.6%–4.5%.)

Schools: Van Horne Elementary, 5855 Ontario Street, grades K-7, School District 39 Vancouver; confirm the catchment with the district. Osler Elementary, 5970 Selkirk Street, grades K-7, School District 39 Vancouver; confirm the catchment with the district. Sir Winston Churchill Secondary, 7055 Heather Street, grades 8-12, School District 39 Vancouver; confirm the catchment with the district.
Shopping: Oakridge Park shopping centre, 650 West 41st Avenue, at Oakridge–41st Avenue Station. Safeway Oakridge Park, Unit 1505, 650 W. 41st Avenue, per the retailer's own store page.

faq.a: Not as a City local area — the corridor runs through the official areas of South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge under the Cambie Corridor Plan, and the board carries both "Cambie" and "South Cambie" as overlapping searches. Name the official area and the nearest Canada Line station in any offer or listing.

The corridor has four: King Edward, Oakridge–41st Avenue, Langara–49th Avenue and Marine Drive. Chelsea, Livingstone, 35 Park West, Lina and The Charlotte sit between King Edward and Oakridge–41st; Forty Nine West and The Camellia sit at Langara–49th; Belpark and Cambie Gardens sit at the Marine Drive end.
faq.q: Which station is my building actually near?

faq.a: Yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration still applies if the unit sits empty instead.
faq.q: Can I rent out a corridor condo long-term?

faq.a: Only partly: OPAL is a 130-home retirement community of which 44 homes are strata condos (the rest are rental and complex-care suites), listings record Freehold Strata title and a 55+ requirement ("One resident must be 55+"), and it operates as a retirement residence — read the service and care agreements, not just the Form B.
faq.q: Is OPAL a normal condo purchase?

faq.a: Oakridge Park (QuadReal and Westbank) is redeveloping the former Oakridge Centre site at 650 West 41st Avenue into a 28-acre mixed-use town centre with 3,000+ homes planned; the first five residential towers (700 strata condos plus 180 social housing units) are reported as expected ready in early 2027. Presale purchases there carry REDMA's 7-day rescission right and GST as new construction.

Not as a City local area — the corridor runs through the official areas of South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge under the Cambie Corridor Plan, and the board carries both "Cambie" and "South Cambie" as overlapping searches. Name the official area and the nearest Canada Line station in any offer or listing.

Two known: Aperture (759 West 41st Avenue, concrete townhomes, Freehold Strata, built 2017) at the Oakridge node, and Winona Park Chateau Parkside Residences (344 West 62nd Avenue, 19 townhomes by Formwerks) at the Marine Drive end.
faq.q: What standalone townhouse complexes exist in the corridor?

faq.a: No. Those are townhouse-form units inside apartment-form strata developments (Chelsea: 79 units across two 6-storey buildings, 2021; The Camellia: 2021, townhouse address 6723 Cambie Street; Lina: 2025).
faq.q: A listing calls a Chelsea / Camellia / Lina unit a "townhouse" — is it a townhouse complex?

faq.a: No — the City has 22 official local areas and "Cambie" is not one of them; the Cambie Street corridor runs through the official areas of South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge under the Cambie Corridor Plan.
faq.q: Is Cambie an official City of Vancouver neighbourhood?

faq.a: The Cambie Corridor Plan, approved by Council on May 9, 2011, guiding growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River around the Canada Line stations, with Phase 3 (2018) extending policy to the surrounding neighbourhood streets.
faq.q: What plan governs the Cambie Street corridor?

faq.a: Townhouse and rowhouse areas, low-rise apartments on the surrounding streets under Phase 3, and medium- to higher-density housing at the station areas, anchored by the Oakridge Municipal Town Centre at 41st and Cambie.
